title: SDK gradual-mode migration and compatibility contract for pagination, retries, and streaming
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: We need a cross-language (Python/TypeScript/Go) contract and rollout plan that allows the SDKs to adopt improved pagination cursors, stronger retry semantics, and a resumable streaming surface without breaking customers. This ticket defines requirements, acceptance criteria, rollout gating, and migration helpers for client libraries so runtime changes and new server-side behaviors can be enabled behind a gradual 'compatibility mode' flag.

Goals:
- Define a single compatibility-mode contract that SDKs can opt into to get new behaviors (cursor tokens, structured streaming events, idempotent retries) while preserving the existing default behavior for the wide tail of users.
- Produce explicit API surface-level specs for Python/TS/Go explaining defaults, opt-in flags, and migration helpers (adapters, shims).
- Provide test matrices and acceptance criteria so runtime and SDK teams can coordinate safe rollout and automated verification.

Non-goals:
- Implementations of the SDK adapters (this ticket stops at spec + acceptance test suite).
- Changes to server-side token formats that cannot be backward-compatible via shims.
requirements:
1) Compatibility mode flag: introduce 'compat_mode' boolean in SDK constructors and a runtime header X-Redwood-Compat: <version> to negotiate features.

2) Pagination:
- Cursor contract: cursors are opaque strings. New mode will support structured cursor metadata (versioned). SDKs must expose a Cursor.decode_safe() helper that returns original cursor if unknown or falls back to legacy page offset semantics.
- Page iterator: provide a .pages() async iterator for TS/Python and channel-based generator for Go. Iterators must preserve stable ordering and document when pages may be combined due to server batching.

3) Retries and idempotency:
- Define retry categories: idempotent (safe to retry), retryable-non-idempotent (requires request-id), non-retryable.
- SDKs must expose a RequestId field (UUID v4) and surface a client-side guarantee: when compat_mode=true SDK will send X-Request-Id and automatically attach it to retry attempts.
- Backoff policy: default is exp-backoff with jitter, max attempts 5 in compat_mode, 3 in legacy. SDKs must allow override.

4) Streaming:
- Streaming envelope versioning: streams will use frame header 'v' with numeric version. Compat_mode enables 'resumable_tokens' field in stream frames.
- Client cancelation and resume: define a resume token format and client API: stream.resume(token) and stream.cancel(). If resume token absent, SDK must fall back to restart from beginning.
- Partial aggregation: SDKs must provide a buffered_stream API to yield partial records with watermarking for ordered consumption.

5) Deprecation and deprecation visibility: SDKs must log a one-time warning when a deprecated surface is used. Deprecation windows and migration docs must be surfaced in SDK release notes and console announcements.

6) Telemetry: SDKs must emit minimal telemetry events (compat_mode enabled, retry_count per call, stream_resume_attempt) to customer-owned telemetry endpoints and to the Redwood console via telemetry opt-in.
acceptance_criteria: Spec document signed off by Runtime, SDK leads (Python/TS/Go), and Product: clear definitions for cursor, resume token, and retry categories.
Automated compatibility test harness (proto) exists: can exercise legacy server semantics and new compat server semantics and validate SDKs respect flags in both directions.
SDK API sketches for Python/TS/Go demonstrating constructor flag, page iterator, request id plumbing, and stream.resume() accepted by SDK leads.

Backward-compat tests: a) SDK with compat_mode=false works unchanged against compat-enabled runtime; b) SDK with compat_mode=true interoperates with legacy runtime with graceful fallback for cursors/resume tokens.
Integration tests that validate idempotent retry behavior with request-id propagation and that non-idempotent operations are not retried by default.
Documentation: migration guide + code snippets for three client languages checked in to docs repo and a short dashboard announcement draft for console release notes.
Rollout plan with gating metrics: error-rate delta < 0.5% on staging and canary, resume-success-rate > 95%, no regressions in end-to-end latency beyond 10% for streaming paths.
A clear deprecation schedule for legacy cursor formats (if any) and a rollback plan with specific toggles for runtime and SDKs.
migration_notes: Provide a 'compat_shim' npm/pip/go package that SDKs can optionally import while full SDK refactors are done. Shim responsibilities: decode new cursor format, inject X-Request-Id, translate resumable frames into legacy events when needed. Shims must be versioned and semver-major aligned with SDK releases. Migration plan phases: 1) spec + tests (this ticket), 2) shims and SDK prototypes in canary, 3) staged rollout with feature flag 'compat_v2' controlled by runtime, 4) deprecate legacy behavior after 6 months of stable metrics.
